```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))   # analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations -> analysis
os.chdir("..")                                # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import laplacelib as R
import truth as T

bins, reps, comps = T.load()
```

Every arm is scored against the simulated truth: first per scenario relative to CAVI-Q2
(@sec-vs-cavi), then pooled over scenarios. The [agreement page](pip_agreement.qmd) compares
arms with CAVI-Q2 directly, replicate by replicate.

- Designs: *Binary* (binary Markov sets, 022), *Binary-Block* (nested binary blocks, 024),
  *Gaussian* (Gaussian AR(1), 023). $L^* = 3$ causals fit at $L = 5$; one causal fit at
  $L = 1$ (the `-ser` grids). 200 replicates per cell, pooled over each design's sweep axis,
  $T$ and gap.
- Declared credible set: the 95% CS of a component with log BF $\geq 2$. A CS covers when it
  contains a causal feature.
- Signal cells only, except where a column says null. gIBSS-GO, Taylor2 and MacKay run at
  $L = 5$ only.
- Source: the pipeline's `pip` and `cs` reductions (`truth.py`).

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
st = (reps.group_by("design", "L", "method")
      .agg((~pl.col("null")).sum().alias("signal"), pl.col("null").sum().alias("null")))
for e in T.EXPS:
    for L in (5, 1):
        g = st.filter((pl.col("design") == T.DESIGN[e]) & (pl.col("L") == L))
        if g.height:
            print(f"- {T.DESIGN[e]}, L={L}: {g['signal'].max()} signal and {g['null'].max()} null "
                  f"fits per arm, {g.height} arms")
```

## Relative to CAVI-Q2, per scenario {#sec-vs-cavi}

Pooled metrics mostly reflect which scenarios are easy. Here each scenario (one grid cell:
design, $L$, sweep value, $T$, gap; signal cells only) gives one number per arm, the arm's
metric minus CAVI-Q2's in the same scenario, on the same replicates. Size is a ratio.

Coverage, power and mean size of declared 95% CSs (component log BF $\geq 2$), as in
@sec-cs.

Scenarios with few declared CSs give noisy coverage differences.

```{python}
#| label: setup-vs-cavi
#| include: false
sf = T.scenario_frame(reps)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-vs-cavi
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Left: CAVI-Q2's own coverage (dashed: nominal 0.95), power and mean CS size, one point per scenario. Right, L = 5 and L = 1: each arm against CAVI-Q2 in the same scenario (dashed: no difference). Colour = arm, marker = design (Binary, Binary-Block, Gaussian). Black bar: median over all scenarios of all three designs (geometric median for sizes and size ratios)."
T.vs_cavi_figure(sf);
```

```{python}
#| label: tab-vs-cavi
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
for col, ratio, head, leg in [
    ("d_coverage", False, "Coverage minus CAVI-Q2", "declared 95% CS coverage, arm minus CAVI-Q2"),
    ("d_power", False, "Power minus CAVI-Q2", "declared 95% CS power, arm minus CAVI-Q2"),
    ("r_size", True, "Mean CS size over CAVI-Q2", "mean declared 95% CS size, arm over CAVI-Q2 (geometric median)"),
]:
    print(f"**{head}**\n")
    print(T.md(T.vs_cavi_table(sf, col, ratio), "cell", "{}",
               legend=f"Each arm column: median [min, max] over scenarios of the {leg}."))
    print()
```

## PIP calibration {#sec-calibration}

```{python}
#| label: fig-calibration-l5
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "L = 5: share of features that are causal (y) per PIP bin (x, 20 bins), signal cells pooled. Dot area grows with the bin's feature count. Dotted line: calibrated."
T.calibration_figure(bins, 5);
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-calibration-l1
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "L = 1: as above."
T.calibration_figure(bins, 1);
```

```{python}
#| label: tab-calibration
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
cal = T.calibration_table(bins, 0.9)
print(T.md(cal.with_columns(pl.format("{} / {}", pl.col("pip").round(3), pl.col("causal").round(3)).alias("cell")),
           "cell", "{}",
           legend="Features with PIP ≥ 0.9, signal cells. Each arm column: mean PIP / share causal. "
                  "Share causal below mean PIP = PIPs too high."))
```

## FDP and power {#sec-fdp}

Select every feature with PIP $\geq t$. FDP is the share of selected features that are not
causal; power is the share of causal features selected.

```{python}
#| label: fig-fdp-power
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Power against FDP as the PIP threshold t sweeps from 1 down to 0, signal cells pooled (so FDP here is pooled over fits). Dots: t = 0.95. Dotted line: FDP = 0.05."
T.fdp_power_figure(bins);
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-fdp-power-04
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "As above, FDP up to 0.4."
T.fdp_power_figure(bins, max_fdp=0.4);
```

```{python}
#| label: tab-fdp
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
for t in (0.95, 0.5):
    tab = T.threshold_table(reps, t).with_columns(
        pl.format("{} / {} / {}", pl.col("fdr").round(3), pl.col("power").round(3),
                  pl.col("null_any").round(3)).alias("cell"))
    print(f"**PIP ≥ {t:g}**\n")
    print(T.md(tab, "cell", "{}",
               legend=f"Each arm column: FDR / power / null. *FDR*: mean over signal fits of the fit's FDP "
                      f"at PIP ≥ {t:g} (0 if nothing is selected). *power*: share of causal features with "
                      f"PIP ≥ {t:g}. *null*: share of null fits that select any feature."))
    print()
```

```{python}
#| label: tab-cs
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
cs = T.cs_table(reps, comps)
specs = [
    ("coverage", "{:.3f}", "Coverage", "share of declared 95% CSs that contain a causal feature (nominal 0.95)."),
    ("power", "{:.3f}", "Power", "share of causal features inside some declared 95% CS."),
    ("mean_size", "{:.1f}", "Mean CS size", "mean size of declared 95% CSs."),
    ("median_size", "{:.0f}", "Median CS size", "median size of declared 95% CSs."),
    ("cs_per_fit", "{:.2f}", "Declared CSs per fit", "declared CSs per signal fit (3 causals at L = 5, 1 at L = 1)."),
    ("null_cs_per_fit", "{:.3f}", "Declared CSs per null fit", "declared CSs per null fit; every one is a false discovery."),
]
for col, fmt, head, leg in specs:
    print(f"**{head}**\n")
    print(T.md(cs, col, fmt, legend=f"Each arm column: {leg}"))
    print()
```
